rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon tells the hoopoe to withdraw from the queen's company, hide nearby, and listen to the reply.
rows.anchor: أعرض عنهم بترك وليهم وقربهم وتبعد إلى مكان تتوارى فيه وتسمع ما يجيبونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to look means to reflect and find out.
rows.anchor: فانظر} تأمل وتعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply in question is what the people say back and forth to one another.
rows.anchor: أي ماذا يرجع بعضهم إلى بعض من القول

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh parses ماذا either as an interrogative noun governed by يرجعون, or as مبتدأ plus ذا بمعنى الذي, with a deleted relative pronoun object.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : ماذا اسم واحد استفهام منصوب بيرجعون أو مبتدأ وذا بمعنى الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the hoopoe found Bilqis asleep in her palace at Ma'rib, with doors locked and keys beneath her head.
rows.anchor: روي : أن الهدهد أخذ الكتاب وأتى بلقيس فوجدها راقدة في قصرها بمأرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoopoe entered through an opening, dropped the letter on Bilqis's chest, withdrew, and startled her awake.
rows.anchor: فدخل من كوة وألقى الكتاب على نحرها وهي مستلقية وتأخر يسيرا فانتبهت فزعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bilqis could read and write Arabic and descended from Tubba al-Himyari.
rows.anchor: وكانت قارئة كاتبة عربية من نسل تبع الحميري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the seal made Bilqis tremble and submit; she judged Solomon the greater king because birds obeyed him and his seal looked imposing.
rows.anchor: فلما رأت الخاتم ارتعدت وخضعت لأن ملك سليمان كان في خاتمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bilqis addresses her leading people, whose number is given as either 313 or twelve thousand.
rows.anchor: لأشراف قومها وهم ثلاثمائة وثلاثة عشر أو اثنا عشر ألفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ملأ are the community's dignitaries, who fill eyes with awe and hearts with majesty; their plural is أملاء.
rows.anchor: والملأ عظماء القوم الذين يملؤون العيون مهابة والقلوب جلالة جمعه أملاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She calls the letter noble because it is honored by her, sealed with a remarkable seal, and delivered in an unusual manner.
rows.anchor: مكرم على معظم لدي لكونه مختوما بخاتم عجيب وأصلا على نهج غير معتاد

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: Al-As'ila al-Muqahima says Solomon's miracle was in his ring: sealing with it displayed his sovereignty and cast fear into Bilqis's heart.
rows.anchor: معجزة سليمان كانت في خاتمه فختم الكتاب بالخاتم الذي فيه ملكه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that a letter's nobility lies in its seal.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : "كرم الكتاب ختمه"

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A version from Ibn Abbas adds the verse in which Bilqis calls the letter noble; al-Sakhawi records it in al-Maqasid al-Hasana.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس بزيادة وهو قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that Muhammad adopted a silver seal ring engraved Muhammad, Messenger of God, because non-Arabs would not accept an unsealed letter.
rows.anchor: على ما رواه أنس رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying warns that an unsealed letter is defeated.
rows.anchor: ويقال : كل كتاب لا يكون مختوما فهو مغلوب

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Jalalayn interprets noble as meaning that the letter's contents are good.
rows.anchor: كريم أي حسن ما فيه انتهى

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh offers two senses: pleasing in wording and meaning, or noble because it begins with the basmala.
rows.anchor: كما قال ابن الشيخ في أوائل سورة الشعراء : كتاب كريم أي مرضي في لفظه ومعانيه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An anonymous couplet praises God's name as the best opening for a letter and as adornment of names and comfort for hearts.
rows.anchor: كما قال بعضهم : (ون مضمون نامه نام خداوند بوده

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading says Bilqis called the letter noble because it led her to guidance and faith in the Presence of the Generous.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن الكتاب لما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say honoring the letter brought Bilqis guidance, as the magicians gained faith by showing Moses proper respect.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : لاحترامها الكتاب رزقت الهداية حتى آمنت كالسحرة لما قدموا في قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Khosrow tore the Prophet's letter, God tore apart his kingdom as punishment for disbelief and defiance.
rows.anchor: ولما مزق كسرى كتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مزق الله ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bilqis's wording answers the implied questions of who sent the letter and what it contains.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل : ممن هو وماذا مضمونه؟ فقالت : إنه من سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An esoteric letter-by-letter reading assigns ba to permanence, sin to splendor, mim to sovereignty, alif to oneness, the two lams to beauty and majesty, and ha to divine identity.
rows.anchor: الباء بقاؤه والسين سناؤه والميم ملكه والألف أحديته واللامان جماله وجلاله والهاء هويته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this reading, al-Rahman signifies mercy to all people in this world and the next, while al-Rahim signifies special mercy in the next world.
rows.anchor: الرحمان إشارة إلى رحمته لأهل العموم في الدنيا والآخرة والرحيم إشارة إلى رحمته لأهل الخصوص في الآخرة

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some great Sufis say this is, in truth, the basmala of Bara'a; because its people were disavowed, it was bestowed on the animals who believed in Solomon.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : إنها بسملة براءة في الحقيقة ولكن لما وقع التبري من أهلها أعطيت للبهائم التي آمنت بسليمان

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: The opening ba suffices because every existent thing is encompassed by God's general or particular mercy.
rows.anchor: واكتفى في أول السورة بالباء إذ كل شيء في الوجود الكوني لا يخلو من رحمة الله عامة أو خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This basmala is not a complete verse like the basmala in Hud, whereas the basmalas opening surahs are separate verses revealed 114 times, once for each surah.
rows.anchor: وهذه البسملة ليست بآية تامة مثل : {بسم الله مجارااها ومرسااهآ} (هود : 41)

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: Jami's Persian couplet says the basmala's nineteen letters pour abundant grace over seventeen thousand worlds.
rows.anchor: قال المولى الجامي في حق البسملة : نوزده حرفست كه هده هزار عالم ازو يافته فيض عميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanatory particle introduces a ban on arrogance, like the behavior of tyrannical kings.
rows.anchor: لا تتكبروا كما يفعل جبابرة الملوك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coming as Muslims means coming as believers and submitters; faith does not necessarily entail submission, while submission entails faith.
rows.anchor: حال كونكم مؤمنين فإن الإيمان لا يستلزم الإسلام والانقياد دون العكس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says prophets used to write concise statements rather than lengthy letters.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : وكذلك كانت الأنبياء عليهم السلام تكتب جملا لا تطيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brief letter's demand for Islam did not precede proof of Solomon's messengership or invite blind imitation; its extraordinary delivery clearly proved the sender's mission.
rows.anchor: وليس الأمر فيه بالإسلام قبل إقامة الحجة على رسالته حتى يتوهم كونه استدعاء للتقليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says necessary knowledge of a messenger's truth is enough; otherwise Bilqis might have attributed the delivery and other marvels, including the throne, to jinn, since her mother was a jinni.
rows.anchor: يكفي في هذا الباب حصول العلم الضروري بصدق الرسول وإلا فهي لا تستبعد كون الإلقاء المذكور بتصرف من الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tilawa is sequential recitation like study or regular litanies; qira'a is broader, and tilawa literally follows without interruption by unrelated material.
rows.anchor: التلاوة قراءة القرآن متتابعة كالدراسة والأوراد الموظفة والقراءة أعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to persist in reciting so that reflection gradually uncovers truths and new meanings previously hidden.
rows.anchor: وأمرت بأن أواظب على تلاوته لتكشف لي حقائقه في تلاوته شيئا فشيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explains why learned sages never tire of Quran recitation: fresh meanings continually appear.
rows.anchor: فإنه كلما تفكر التالي العالم تجلت له معان جديدة كانت في حجب مخفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quran recitation is the final regular devotional portion because knowers first uncover the realities of the horizons, then the self, then the Quran.
rows.anchor: كان آخر وردهم لأن المنكشف أولا للعارفين حقائق الآفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone should recite daily; students and some Sufis wrongly abandon it while claiming more important pursuits, although the Quran is the basis of every worldly science.
rows.anchor: فعليك بتلاوة القرآن كل يوم ولا تهجره كما يفعل ذلك طلبة العلم وبعض المتصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reader from the codex should recite aloud and place a hand on the verse, giving the tongue, eye, and hand their respective acts of raising, seeing, and touching.
rows.anchor: ويستحب لقارىء القرآن في المصحف أن يجهر بقراءته ويضع يده على الآية يتبعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing the Quran is the most honored and highest provision of the angels who travel about.
rows.anchor: وسماع القرآن أشرف أرزاق الملائكة السياحين وأعلاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those unable to recite should attend knowledge gatherings for the spirits, while keeping their study within Quranic sciences.
rows.anchor: ومن لم تتيسر له تلاوة القرآن فليجلس لبث العلم لأجل الأرواح الذين غذاؤهم العلم لكن لا يتعدى علوم القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ears' inward purification is hearing good speech, with Quranic remembrance of God the highest form; not every verse explicitly mentions God, though listening to any Quran brings reward.
rows.anchor: والطهارة الباطنة للأذنين تكون باستماع القول الحسن فإنه ثم حسن وأحسن فأعلاه حسنا ذكر الله بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's character was the Quran: enact or resolve to enact every praised quality and abandon or resolve to abandon every condemned one, since revelation calls for practice.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن خلق النبي عليه السلام كان القرآن فانظر في تلاوتك إلى كل صفة مدح الله بها عباده فافعلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The complete person preserves the Quran from neglected practice as well as from errors in recitation.
rows.anchor: فإذا حفظت القرآن عن تضييع العمل به كما حفظته تلاوة فأنت الرجل الكامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance means following the Prophet in worship, Islam, and Quran recitation, and its benefit returns to the guided person alone.
rows.anchor: باتباعه إياي فيما ذكر من العبادة والإسلام وتلاوة القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever opposes these teachings is astray; the Prophet has discharged his duty by warning, and bears no responsibility for the person's outcome.
rows.anchor: فقد خرجت من عهدة الإنذار والتخويف من عذاب الله وسخطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command means to keep reciting the Quran to people through repeated calls; then guidance means faith and observance of its laws, and error means rejecting it and its practice.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معنى وأن أتلو القرآن وأن أواظب على تلاوته للناس بطريق تكرير الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this verse was abrogated by the sword verse.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية منسوخة بآية السيف

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading likens Quranic light cultivating guidance and error in the human heart to sunlight maturing gold and iron in mines.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : فيه إشارة إلى أن نور القرآن

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: It adduces the statement that God leads many astray and guides many, and the Prophetic saying that people are like mines of gold and silver.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه قوله تعالى : {يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise is due for the blessings God bestowed, above all prophethood and the Quran.
rows.anchor: أي على ما أفاض علي من نعمائه التي أجلها نعمة النبوة والقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming signs will be recognized as God's signs when recognition can no longer benefit their observers.
rows.anchor: أي فتعرفون أنها آيات الله حين لا تنفعكم المعرفة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid? The source names Muqatil: the signs will appear soon, so blessed is whoever returns before death and doomed whoever returns after the opportunity passes.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : سيريكم آياته عن قريب الأيام فطوبى لمن رجع قبل وفاته

rows.speaker: سعدي
rows.claim: Sa'di's poem urges the sleeper to wake and repent while time remains, before death or opportunity's flood has passed.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره : كنون بايد أي خفته بيدار بود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is God's speech, reinforcing the prior promise and threat; the shift from addressing the Prophet to addressing unbelievers signals this.
rows.anchor: كلام مسوق من جهته تعالى مقرر لما قبله من الوعد والوعيد كما ينبىء عنه إضافة الرب إلى ضمير النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not unaware of the Prophet's good deeds or unbelievers' sins; He recompenses each, knows them as their creator, and delays punishment for wisdom.
rows.anchor: وما ربك بغافل عما تعمل أنت من الحسنات وما تعملون أنتم أيها الكفرة من السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine heedlessness is impossible because forgetfulness is a lapse caused by weak vigilance, unlike God's perfect knowledge.
rows.anchor: لأن الغفلة التي هي سهو يعتري من قلة التحفظ والتيقظ لا يجوز عليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truly heedless person is someone who fails to notice this truth and persists in associating partners with God and committing sins.
rows.anchor: وإنما الغفلة لمن لا يتنبه لهذا فيعصي الله بالشرك وسيئات الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting God is among the gravest diseases of the heart, and remembrance is its proper remedy.
rows.anchor: وأعظم الأمراض القلبية نسيان الله ولا ريب أن علاج أمر إنما هو بضده وهو ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham dreamed of a book warning him not to prefer the perishing world or trust his kingdom, and urging him to hasten toward God's forgiveness and Paradise.
rows.anchor: سر يوما بمملكته ونعمته ثم نام فرأى رجلا أعطاه كتابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He awoke frightened, took the dream as divine admonition, repented, and abandoned delay and idleness on the path of truth.
rows.anchor: فانتبه فزعا وقال : هذا تنبيه من الله وموعظة فتاب إلى الله ورسوله بالقبول والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian maxim says no one finds ease without enduring effort.
rows.anchor: براحتي نرسيد آنكه زحمتي نكشيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses entered Misr after coming from Pharaoh's palace, which stood at the city's edge.
rows.anchor: ودخل موسى مصرا آتيا من قصر فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the palace's location to the later reference to a man arriving from the far side of the city.
rows.anchor: كما سيأتي عند قوله تعالى : {وجآء رجل من أقصا المدينة} (القصص : 20)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the city as Memphis, Pharaoh's residence: it lay west of the Nile, twelve miles from old Cairo, and was Egypt's royal seat and earliest post-Flood city.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد مدينة منف من أرض مصر وهي مدينة فرعون موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time was one when people did not normally enter the city.
rows.anchor: أي حال كونه في وقت لا يعتاد دخولها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses entered at midday during the customary rest, when the roads were empty.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : دخلها في الظهيرة عند المقيل وقد خلت الطرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the two men fighting describes رجلين as an adjective clause.
rows.anchor: الجملة صفة لرجلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb form اقتتال means that the men fought one another.
rows.anchor: والاقتتال (كارزار كردن بايكديكر)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man from Moses's faction was one who followed him in religion, namely an Israelite.
rows.anchor: أي ممن شايعه وتابعه على دينه وهم بنو إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fath al-Rahman reports that the Israelite was the Samaritan.
rows.anchor: روي أنه السامري كما في "فتح الرحمن"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative wording retells the scene: the men were not present when the Prophet heard the account, but were present when Moses encountered them.
rows.anchor: والإشارة على الحكاية وإلا فهو والذي من عدوه ما كانا حاضرين حال الحكاية لرسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's religious opponents were Copts; Kashf al-Asrar names this man Fatun and says he was Pharaoh's baker trying to force an Israelite to carry wood to the royal kitchen.
rows.anchor: وهم القبط واسمه فاتون كما في "كشف الأسرار" وكان خباز فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite asked Moses for help against the Copt; على governs the request because استغاث means seeking aid or support.
rows.anchor: أي سأله أن يغيثه بالإعانة عليه ولذلك عدي بعلي يقال : استغثت طلبت الغوث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses had been given strength and power.
rows.anchor: وكان موسى قد أعطي شدة وقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian gloss says Moses told the Copt to release the man, but the Copt rejected Moses's words.
rows.anchor: قبطي راكفت دست ازو بدار قبطي سخن موسى ردكرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wakz can mean pushing, thrusting, or striking with the closed fist; Moses struck the Copt with his fist.
rows.anchor: الوكز كالوعد الدفع والطعن والضرب بجمع الكف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses killed the Copt, regretted it, and buried him in sand; قضيت عليه can also mean finishing or completing something.
rows.anchor: أي : فقتله فندم فدفنه في الرمل وكل شيء فرغت وأتممته فقد قضيت عليه

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat explains that death is expressed with القضاء, as in completing one's allotted term, since it ends one's distinct worldly affair.
rows.anchor: في "المفردات" : يعبر عن الموت بالقضاء فيقضى نحبه لأنه فصل أمره بالمختص به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses attributes the killing to Satan because it arose through Satan's misleading and whispering.
rows.anchor: فأضيف العمل إلى الشيطان لأنه كان بإغوائه ووسوسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It was Satan's work because Moses had not been ordered to kill unbelievers, or because he was safe among them and should not have assassinated one.
rows.anchor: وإنما كان من عمله لأنه لم يؤمر بقتل الكفار أو لأنه كان مأمونا فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the act injustice and asking forgiveness does not compromise infallibility: it was an error before prophethood, and the elect magnify even minor lapses.
rows.anchor: ولا يقدح ذلك في عصمته لكونه خطأ وإنما عده من عمل الشيطان وسماه ظلما واستغفر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Satan, Adam's enemy and an evident adversary who leads people astray.
rows.anchor: لابن آدم {مضل مبين} ظاهر العداوة والإضلال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing قال between Moses's statements signals the contrast between the first utterance and the later intimate prayer.
rows.anchor: توسيط قال بين كلاميه لإبانة ما بينهما من المخالفة من حيث أنه مناجاة ودعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he wronged himself by killing the Copt without command, asks forgiveness, and receives it in response to his repentance.
rows.anchor: بقتل القبطي بغير أمر {فاغفر لى} ذنبي {فغفر له} ربه ذلك لاستغفاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghafur and al-Rahim describe God as exceedingly forgiving of servants' sins and merciful to them.
rows.anchor: المبالغ في مغفرة ذنوب العباد ورحمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading treats the phrase as an oath by God's favor of forgiveness, with the implied response that Moses will surely repent.
rows.anchor: إما قسم محذوف الجواب أي أقسم عليك بإنعامك علي بالمغفرة لأتوبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses appeals to God's kindness to protect him from helping anyone whose aid leads to wrongdoing and severance from God.
rows.anchor: وإما استعطاف أي بحق إحسانك علي اعصمني فلن أكون معينا لمن تؤدي معاونته إلى الجرم

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says one who knows God's blessings will not side with someone who opposes the Benefactor, and one who knows the Benefactor will never oppose him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : العارف بنعم الله من لا يوافق من خالف ولي نعمته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses did not make an exception, so he was later tested by helping criminals again.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه لم يستثن فابتلي به أي بالعون للمجرمين مرة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here a criminal means anyone who commits a blameworthy act; the Israelite need not be an unbeliever, since Israelites followed Jacob's religion before Moses and were enslaved by Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: المراد بالمجرم ههنا الجاني الكاسب فعلا مذموما فلا يلزم أن يكون الإسرائيلي كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas's interpretation as helping unbelievers shows that the generic label criminal may be applied to a sinful believer as emphatic rebuke.
rows.anchor: قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عند قوله : ظهيرا للمجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This prayer is apt amid disputes over religion, rule, or other matters; Moses used it during the fight, and Ibn Umar used it during the conflict between Ali and Muawiya, as Kashf al-Asrar reports.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال موسى هذا عند اقتتال الرجلين ودعا به ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما عند قتال علي ومعاوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The esoteric reading calls people who combat the soul's natural traits through desire instead of revealed law and following, such as philosophers, Brahmins, and monks, criminals; their struggle is satanic.
rows.anchor: إن المجرمين هم الذين أجرموا بأن جاهدوا كفار صفات النفس بالطبع والهوى لا بالشرع والمتابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ottoman sultans are the final dynasty and will continue into the time of the awaited Mahdi, according to what major scholars have established as sound.
rows.anchor: ومن الملوك الخواقين العثمانية لأن دولتهم آخر الدول وتتصل بزمان المهدي المنتظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors scholars who unite outward and inward knowledge, and prays for steadfastness on the path of realization.
rows.anchor: واختار من العلماء من تشرف بعلم الظاهر والباطن وكان ذا جناحين نسأل الله الثبات في طريق التحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what hearts conceal, such as hostility toward the Messenger and resentment of believers; أكننت means hidden within oneself, while كننت means covered by a physical object.
rows.anchor: أي تضمر قلوبهم وتخفي كعداوة الرسول وحقد المؤمنين يقال : أكننت الشيء إذا أخفيته في نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people make public includes speech and bodily actions such as attacking prophethood and denying the Quran.
rows.anchor: {وما يعلنون} بألسنتهم وجوارحهم كالطعن في النبوة وتكذيب القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God deserves worship; He alone possesses divinity and lordship, with no equal or comparable being.
rows.anchor: لا أحد يستحقها إلا هو وهو المتوحد بعز إلهيته المتفرد بجلال ربوبيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God deserves praise for His greatness and thanks for His favors in this world and the next, since He grants every present and future blessing to all creation.
rows.anchor: استحقاقا على عظمته والشكر استيجابا على نعمته {فى الاولى} أي الدنيا {والاخرة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers will praise God in the afterlife with joy and delight, without burden.
rows.anchor: يحمده المؤمنون في الآخرة كما حمدوه في الدنيا بقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone has the effective decree over what He creates, chooses, honors, humiliates, gives life to, and causes to die.
rows.anchor: فيما يخلق ويختار ويعز ويذل ويحيي ويميت أي القضاء النافذ في كل شيء

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar says God's effective judgment governs both worlds and all creatures ultimately return to His judgment in the next.
rows.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : وله الحكم النافذ في الدنيا والآخرة ومصير الخلق كلهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God decrees forgiveness for the obedient and misery and woe for the disobedient.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : حكم لأهل طاعته بالمغفرة ولأهل معصيته بالشقاء والويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people return to God through resurrection, and to no other.
rows.anchor: بالبعث لا إلى غيره

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading distinguishes a voluntary return through spiritual journey, following, and arrival in the Divine Presence, reserved for humans, from an involuntary return through death, resurrection, judgment, and recompense.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {وإليه ترجعون} بالاختيار أو بالاضطرار فأما بالاختيار فهو الرجوع إلى الحضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address honors believers unable to establish religious duties fully because of obstruction from unbelievers and guides them to the safer course.
rows.anchor: خطاب تشريف لبعض المؤمنين الذين لا يتمكنون من إقامة أمور الدين كما ينبغي لممانعة من جهة الكفر

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi reports that some believers remained in caves instead of migrating because of scant provisions, limited means, attachment to homeland or family, and fear while worshipping.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (آورده اندكه جمعي ازمؤمنان دركمه اقامت كرده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If worship or public practice of religion is not possible in one country, believers should migrate to a place where it is possible.
rows.anchor: العبادة في بلد ولم يتيسر لكم اظهار دينكم فهاجروا إلى حيث يتمشى لكم ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth means the created terrestrial realm: the lands and places God made.
rows.anchor: الأرض الجرم المقابل للسماء أي بلاد المواضع التي خلقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth's breadth means believers are not constrained to one land; if devotion cannot be purified there, they should devote themselves elsewhere, with fronting the object marking exclusivity.
rows.anchor: لا مضايقة لكم فيها فإن لم تخلصوا العبادة لي في أرضي

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi warns that those attached to home and family will eventually have to part from them.
rows.anchor: واكر از دوستى أهل وولد بابسته بلده شده ايد روزى مفارقت ضرورت خواهد بود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated قبل stresses how long people had waited for rain and how firmly they had despaired; مبلسين means hopeless, and the lām distinguishes the predicate.
rows.anchor: تكرير للتأكيد والدلالة على تطاول عهدهم بالمطر واستحكام يأسهم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though addressed to the Prophet, the command to look is meant for all morally responsible people, and God's mercy here means rain.
rows.anchor: الخطاب وإن توجه نحو النبي عليه السلام فالمراد به جميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should see the plants, trees, fruits, and flowers produced by rain; the ف signals how quickly these follow the rainfall.
rows.anchor: من النبات والأشجار وأنواع الثمار والأزهار والفاء للدلالة على سرعة ترتب هذه الأشياء على تنزيل المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God revives the earth through these traces, and its death means its dryness.
rows.anchor: {كيف يحى} أي : الله تعالى {الارض} بالآثار {بعد موتها} أي : يبسها

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad parses كيف as an accusative after removing a preposition and suspended by انظر; the object is the wondrous revival of earth, proving power and mercy and preparing belief in resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : كيف الخ في حيز النصب بنزع الخافض وكيف معلق لانظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who revives earth can resurrect the dead: resurrection brings forth again the animal powers once present in bodily matter, as earthly revival renews its plant powers.
rows.anchor: فإنه إحداث لمثل ما كان في مواد أبدانهم من القوى الحيوانية كما أن إحياء الأرض إحياء لمثل ما كان فيها من القوى النباتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power over all possibilities is equal, including resurrecting the human body and reviving a dead heart in this life; unlike a servant, His power is not dependent on another.
rows.anchor: ومن إحياء قلبه بعد موته في الدنيا لأن نسبة قدرته إلى جميع الممكنات على سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet praises God as the living, knowing One who gives strength to every weak person.
rows.anchor: تعالى الله زهى قيوم ودانا توانايى ده هر ناتوانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God adorns the earth with signs of His power, action, and wisdom; gnostics behold divine manifestation through its visible forms.
rows.anchor: زين الأرض بآثار قدرته وأنوار فعله وحكمته فأنبت الخضرة وأضاء الزهر

rows.speaker: الشيخ المغربي
rows.claim: A couplet attributed to al-Maghribi says every garden's color and fragrance are his own color and fragrance.
rows.anchor: مغربي زان ميكند ميلى بكلشن كاندر او هره را رنكى وبويى هست رنك وبوى اوست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites asked Moses if his Lord dyes; he said God colors fruits and flowers, and unlike human dyers can turn black hair and a black heart white, as the verse about God's coloring says.
rows.anchor: وسأل بنو إسرائيل موسى عليه السلام : هل يصبغ ربك؟ قال : نعم يصبغ ألوان الثمار والرياحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hafs went to a garden in obedience to this verse; when a Magian hosted him and his companions admired the garden, he had them recite the verse about what former people left behind.
rows.anchor: خرج أبو حفص قدس سره إلى البستان ائتمارا بقوله تعالى : {فانظر إلى ءاثار رحمت الله}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Abu Hafs left, the Magian and eighteen relatives converted; Abu Hafs advised taking such spiritually fruitful outings, not going out with appetite and ego, which yield no good result.
rows.anchor: ولما أراد أن يخرج أبو حفص أسلم المجوسي وثمانية عشر من أولاده وأقربائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Look at worldly flowers with the outer eye and their perishability with the heart; draw many lessons from spring and remember resurrection when seeing it, since graves yield the dead as earth yields plants.
rows.anchor: يلزم للإنسان أن ينظر بعين ظاهره إلى زهرة الدنيا وبعين قلبه إلى فنائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report teaches people to remember Judgment's sun in intense heat; one who seeks refuge from Hell's heat by affirming God's oneness is promised protection.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إذا رأيتم الربيع فاذكروا النشور" أي : فإن خروج الموتى من القبور كخروج النبات من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parallel report promises protection to someone who seeks refuge from Hell's bitter cold; Zamharir is described as a freezing house where an unbeliever is cast and disintegrates.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان اليوم شديد البرد فإذا قال العبد لا إله إلا الله ما أشد برد هذا اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain should remind people of sinners weeping on the Bridge.
rows.anchor: وينبغي أن يذكر بكاء العصاة على الصراط عند رؤية نزول المطر من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A scholar wept at a rose, likening its open white to a dead person's remaining eye-whites and saying a widow's remarriage splits the dead husband's heart.
rows.anchor: ونظر بعض العلماء إلى الورد فبكى وقال : إن الميت يبكي في الأرض إلا بياض عينيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An esoteric gloss reads the revived earth as the believer's soul, dried by neglect of devotional acts, renewed by God's mercy.
rows.anchor: ويقال في الآية : {رحمت الله كيف} يعني نفس المؤمن بعد يبوستها من الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says whoever revives dead land owns it; analogously, God revives the believer's soul and heart for Himself, and a penitent who revives the soul through worship belongs to Paradise rather than Hell.
rows.anchor: روي في الخبر "من أحيى أرضا ميتة فهي له" فالله تعالى أحيى نفس المؤمن وقلبه فهو له لا للشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further inward readings say God revives souls after languor through sincere intention, hearts after heedlessness through lights of presence, and spirits after veiling through continuous witnessing.
rows.anchor: ويقال يحيي النفوس بعد فترتها بصدق الإرادات ويحيى القلوب بعد غفلتها بأنوار المحاضرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet says that remembering the beloved brings death and then life again.
rows.anchor: أموت إذا ذكرتك ثم أحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gnostic's heart is a garden and paradise, alive through knowing God; whoever sees its lights needs no worldly garden or flowers.
rows.anchor: والقلب بستان العارف وجنته وحياته بمعرفة الله تعالى فمن نظر إلى أنواره استغنى عن العالم وأزهاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Masnavi poem contrasts a Sufi lost in contemplation with God's command to look at mercy's traces, then says outward gardens reflect inner gardens and fruits of the heart and divine kindness upon the elements.
rows.anchor: صوفى در باغ از بهر كشاد صوفيانه روى بر زانو نهادس فرو رفت او بخود اندر نغول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing prayer asks God to open insight for witnessing mercy and divine attributes, admit the seekers to the garden of the divine essence, and revive their hearts.
rows.anchor: نسأل الله تعالى أن يفتح بصائرنا لمشاهدة آثار رحمته ومطالعة أنوار صفاته
